chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ali ibn Ribat from Hamzah ibn Humran who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Kalalah, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'That which is not a son and not a father'.

key_terms.الْكَلَالَةِ: Kalalah, a person with no direct descendants or ascendants

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of Kalalah in Shia Islamic inheritance law?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi offers a concise definition of 'Kalalah' as an individual lacking both direct descendants (offspring) and direct ascendants (parents), a status that triggers specific inheritance rules in Surah An-Nisa. In Shia jurisprudence, this definition is crucial for determining the distribution of the estate among collateral relatives when the primary line of succession is absent. The narration underscores the precision with which the Imams clarified legal terminology to ensure equitable application of divine law.
